hypotheses.justification: The proof only uses these two instances to show that p ↦ rankAtStalk M p is locally constant, so it can be moved to the generic point ⊥. That step can be skipped. For any prime p of the domain S, p.primeCompl ≤ nonZeroDivisors S, because 0 ∈ p. So the same two rewrites the proof already applies at ⊥ work at p. IsLocalization.rank_eq gives rank_{S_p}(M_p) = rank_S(M_p). IsLocalizedModule.rank_eq, applied to LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.primeCompl M, gives rank_S(M_p) = rank_S M = n. Hence rank_{S_p}(M_p) = n, and rankAtStalk M p is defined as Module.finrank (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) (LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl M). So it equals n by Module.finrank_eq_of_rank_eq. No finite presentation is needed. The statement stays true. IsDomain is still needed: for S = k×k and M = k×0 the rank is 0 but a stalk has rank 1. This can be deleted together with the Flat hypothesis.

Flatness is used only to apply Module.isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk and move from p to ⊥. The rank-of-localization lemmas (IsLocalization.rank_eq and IsLocalizedModule.rank_eq, which need only p.primeCompl ≤ nonZeroDivisors S) hold directly at every prime p of a domain. So rankAtStalk M p = finrank of the localized module = toNat of rank S M = n, with no flatness. It can be deleted, also together with FinitePresentation.
